```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 80)
library(cytokineR)
library(data.table)
```

Every processing step in cytokineR is a *method* registered under one of four
stages. The built-in methods use exactly the same mechanism as yours, so a
new idea can be dropped into pipelines and benchmarked against the existing
ones in a few lines.

```{r}
cyto_methods()
```

## The method contract

A method is a function `function(x, ...)`. It receives the whole
[cyto] object -- `x$data` is a data.table with one row per well x analyte --
plus the arguments the user gave, and returns a list:

* `value` (required): the new working value for every row, on a log2 scale;
* `scale` (optional): `"log2_fi"`, `"log2_ratio"` or `"log2_conc"`;
* `censored`, `limit_low`, `limit_high`, `qc`, `use_for_fit` (optional);
* `columns` (optional): further columns to add;
* `fit` (optional): what was estimated -- stored and returned by
  `cyto_fit()`, which is what keeps every step auditable;
* `note` (optional): a short text for the step log.

Two rules: do not modify `x$data` in place (copy first), and use only rows
with `use_for_fit == TRUE` when estimating anything, so that the benchmark
can hold material out.

## Example 1: a new signal representation

"Multiple of the lowest standard" -- a curve-free scale anchored at the
bottom of the standard curve, which is close to the detection limit and so
often closer to the samples than the blank:

```{r}
mo_lowest <- function(x, ...) {
  d <- x$data
  ref <- d[sample_type == "standard" & use_for_fit & level == max(level, na.rm = TRUE),
           .(ref = mean(log2(fi))), by = .(plate, analyte)]
  r <- merge(d[, .(.row, plate, analyte)], ref, by = c("plate", "analyte"),
             all.x = TRUE)
  setorder(r, .row)
  list(value = log2(d$fi) - r$ref, scale = "log2_ratio", fit = ref,
       note = "log2(FI / lowest standard)",
       censored = rep("none", nrow(d)))
}
register_cyto_method("transform", "mo_lowest", mo_lowest,
                     description = "Multiple of the lowest standard")
x <- cyto_transform(cyto_example, "mo_lowest")
head(cyto_fit(x))
```

## Example 2: a new plate correction

A robust regression of each plate's control levels on the consensus control
levels -- a two-point "affine" anchor with the two control materials:

```{r}
two_point <- function(x, by = "plate", ...) {
  d <- x$data
  a <- d[sample_type == "control" & use_for_fit & is.finite(value),
         .(y = mean(value)), by = c(by, "sample_id", "analyte")]
  a[, target := median(y), by = .(sample_id, analyte)]
  tab <- a[, {
    if (.N == 2 && diff(range(y)) > 0.5) {
      b <- diff(target[order(y)]) / diff(sort(y))
      b <- min(max(b, 0.5), 2)
      list(intercept = mean(target) - b * mean(y), slope = b)
    } else list(intercept = mean(target - y), slope = 1)
  }, by = c(by, "analyte")]
  m <- merge(d[, c(".row", by, "analyte"), with = FALSE], tab,
             by = c(by, "analyte"), all.x = TRUE)
  setorder(m, .row)
  m[is.na(slope), `:=`(intercept = 0, slope = 1)]
  list(value = m$intercept + m$slope * d$value, fit = tab,
       note = "two-point control calibration")
}
register_cyto_method("normalize", "two_point", two_point,
                     description = "Affine map from two control levels")
```

## Benchmark them next to the built-in methods

```{r}
pipes <- list(
  "MoB > bridge" = cyto_pipeline(pipe_transform("mob"),
                                 pipe_correct_batch("bridge")),
  "mo_lowest > bridge" = cyto_pipeline(pipe_transform("mo_lowest"),
                                       pipe_correct_batch("bridge")),
  "log2 > two_point > bridge" = cyto_pipeline(pipe_transform("log2"),
                                              pipe_normalize("two_point"),
                                              pipe_correct_batch("bridge"))
)
folds <- holdout_folds(cyto_example, "bridge", k = 2)
bm <- benchmark_pipelines(cyto_example, pipes, holdout = folds,
                          metrics = default_metrics(bio = ~ time,
                                                    adjust = ~ subject),
                          verbose = FALSE)
bm
```

(The two-point method uses both control materials, so here half of the
bridging samples are held out in turn.)

## Custom metrics

A metric is a function `function(x, holdout)` returning a data frame with
columns `metric`, `analyte`, `value` (and optionally `n`). For example, the
correlation between two analytes that you expect to move together (in this
simulated data they are independent, so the values are near zero):

```{r}
il6_il8 <- function(x, holdout) {
  w <- cyto_wide(x)
  data.frame(metric = "cor_IL6_IL8", analyte = "IL-6/IL-8",
             value = stats::cor(w[["IL-6"]], w[["IL-8"]],
                                use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
}
m <- c(default_metrics(bio = ~ time, adjust = ~ subject),
       list(cor = il6_il8))
bm2 <- benchmark_pipelines(cyto_example, pipes, holdout = folds,
                           metrics = m, verbose = FALSE)
bm2$summary[, .(pipeline, cor_IL6_IL8, mean_rank)]
```

## Custom steps in pipelines

Anything that takes and returns a cyto object can be a pipeline step,
for example a QC filter:

```{r}
p <- cyto_pipeline(
  pipe_custom(function(x) flag_beads(x, min_count = 50), label = "beads50"),
  pipe_custom(function(x) cyto_filter(x, analyte != "IL-1b"), label = "drop IL-1b"),
  pipe_transform("mo_lowest")
)
run_pipeline(cyto_example, p)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
unregister_cyto_method("transform", "mo_lowest")
unregister_cyto_method("normalize", "two_point")
```
